sections.MESSAGE_TO_USER:
**Recommendation: hold [#196561](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561). Don't merge it or add `autosubmit` until a quick reproduction comes back.** It is approved and green, but one of mboetger's comments says our code comment states something false.

I haven't re-queried live PR state in this turn. Before I call it ready again, I'll re-run `pr_triage.dart --threads` and re-fetch reviews and comments.

**mboetger's 3 inline comments** (posted just before his "Overall LGTM"):

1. **[r4606831206](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606831206), `toBigIntegerOrNull()` nit.** This is a style point, not a behavior claim. I won't push a commit just for this, because a push dismisses all 3 approvals and reruns about an hour of presubmits. If we push for comments 2–3 anyway, it goes in the same commit, after the worker confirms the parsing behaves the same for inputs like `+5`, `""` and leading zeros.
2. **[r4606860038](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606860038), 2 comments in one thread.** Our KDoc says APKs built with `force-version-code-ignoring-abi` and no manifest `versionCode` are ones "Android refuses to install." mboetger says:
   - he installed one with `adb`;
   - it only fails when installed over a build that has a `versionCode`.

   **Status: not reproduced.** I expect he's right, since Android defaults a missing `versionCode` to 0. But I won't call this a wording nit until we test it. If he's right, the problem may be bigger than the comment. That reasoning is why the error message doesn't suggest the flag, and the flag does help for local `adb` installs. So the user-facing error text might need to change, not just the KDoc.

**Why hold rather than merge and follow up:** you want this cherry-picked into 3.50 and 3.51. If the error message has to change, a follow-up means a second cherry-pick on each branch, so 4 CPs instead of 2. One push now costs re-approval plus about an hour of CI. If the reproduction shows only the KDoc wording is off, I'll come back and you can choose: one push now with both fixes, or merge as is and fix it later.

**Next steps:**
- I'm sending `matt561` to reproduce on an emulator and record the exact commands and output.
- It will prepare any fix as a local commit only. Nothing gets pushed without your OK.
- mboetger is a human reviewer, so the worker will draft replies locally for you to post. No agent will post in those threads.
- If we do push, I'll run an `adversarial-review` on the fix diff before calling the PR ready.

**Decision 1: Merge timing**
- **1a (recommended):** hold the merge until the reproduction result, then decide whether to push.
- **1b:** merge now and handle the comments in a follow-up PR. This risks a second cherry-pick on each release branch.

Reply "go 1a" to hold, or "go 1b" to merge now.
sections.WORKER_BRIEF:
<WORKER-BRIEF>

**Task: reproduce a reviewer's behavior claim and prepare a fix locally on flutter/flutter#196561. DO NOT PUSH.**

**Context**
- PR: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561, "Fix --split-per-abi versionCode when android {} omits versionCode".
- Branch: `vcfix-manifest-fallback`, head `f3d2ab1fd3b`.
- reidbaker, bkonyi and mboetger have all approved, and CI is green.
- Pushing any commit dismisses all 3 approvals and reruns about an hour of presubmits. The PR will be cherry-picked into 3.50 and 3.51. Commit to a local branch only. The coordinator and the user decide whether to push.
- `force-version-code-ignoring-abi` is a Gradle property (`-P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`). It skips this PR's per-ABI versionCode logic entirely.

**Reviewer comments (mboetger, a human reviewer, quoted exactly)**

Comment 1, `ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt` line 113, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606831206:
> nit: toBigIntegerOrNull() exists

It is on:
```kotlin
val versionCode =
    try {
        BigInteger(value)
    } catch (e: NumberFormatException) {
        null
    }
```

Comments 2 and 3, one thread on `ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt` line 152, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606860038:
> I don't think this is true.  Can't submit to Play Store sure - but I was able to install with adb.

> I believe it will reject if you try to install over a build with a versionCode.

The thread is on the KDoc of `errorMessage(variantName, reason)`. That KDoc says the error doesn't suggest `force-version-code-ignoring-abi` because "When the manifest has no positive `versionCode`, the flag builds APKs with no `versionCode`, which Android refuses to install. When the value is not a decimal integer, AGP fails the build."

**Claim status: NOT REPRODUCED.** The claim is that an APK with no `versionCode` installs with `adb` on a clean device, and is rejected only when installed over a build that has a `versionCode`. Neither the coordinator nor anyone else has tested this. Reproduce it before you act on it.

**1. Reproduce the claim (on an emulator, preferably 2 API levels: one recent and one near the minSdk)**
1. Set up a Flutter app where `android {}` omits `versionCode` and the manifest has no positive `versionCode`. This is the case where the PR's error fires.
2. Build split-per-ABI APKs with the flag on. Use either:
   - `flutter build apk --split-per-abi` with the project property passed through (for example `-P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true` / `--android-project-arg`), or
   - Gradle directly from `android/`.

   Record the exact command.
3. Inspect each APK's version code with `aapt2 dump badging <apk> | grep -i version` or `apkanalyzer manifest version-code <apk>`. Note whether the attribute is missing or is `0`.
4. Clean install: run `adb uninstall <pkg>`, then `adb install <apk>`. Record the output.
5. Upgrade over a versioned build: install a build with a `versionCode` (for example 1), then `adb install -r <no-versionCode apk>`. Record the output, such as `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE`.
6. Also try the reverse: install the versioned build over the unversioned one.
7. Report every command with its full output. If a step can't be run, say "not reproduced" and why.

**2. Decide whether code, tests, or docs must change**
I haven't decided the fix; give me your recommendation with reasons. In particular:
- If `adb` installs work, is the KDoc only wrong, or is the reasoning behind not suggesting the flag in the user-facing error also wrong?
- Should the error mention the flag with caveats, such as local installs only, no upgrades over versioned builds, and Play rejects the APK?
- Do any tests assert the current message?

You may implement your recommended change as a local commit so we can see the diff, but do not push it.

**3. Comment 1 (`toBigIntegerOrNull()`)**
1. Confirm `String.toBigIntegerOrNull()` is available with the Kotlin version this Gradle plugin uses.
2. Check that it accepts and rejects the same inputs as `BigInteger(value)` with the catch: for example `"5"`, `"+5"`, `"-5"`, `"007"`, `""`, `" 5"`, `"1e3"`, `"0x10"`. Show the evidence (a quick test or a REPL run).
3. If the behavior matches, make the change in the same local commit. If it differs, explain how and recommend keep or change.

**4. Verify locally**
Run the relevant Gradle plugin unit tests and analysis on your local commit. Report the commands and results.

**5. Draft replies (do not post)**
mboetger is a human reviewer, so never post on GitHub. Draft one reply per thread for reidbaker to post. Each reply states the change, or the reason for declining, directly. Mark each comment as changed, modified or declined.

**Report back with:**
- reproduction commands and outputs;
- your recommendation per comment, with reasons;
- `git diff f3d2ab1fd3b..<local-head>`;
- test results;
- the draft replies.

Confirm nothing was pushed.
